stories.head: Only 15% of companies combine agentic AI with cross-departmental orchestration in CX
stories.plain: A Talkdesk report finds 98% of firms have deployed AI in their customer journey, but only 15% have wired it together across departments to actually resolve issues end-to-end. This orchestration gap is the core reason AI CX investments are not paying off — a critical benchmark for anyone buying or building agentic customer experience systems.

stories.head: Auxia hits 200B+ decisions and launches Agent Studio for marketing teams
stories.plain: Auxia, an agentic marketing platform, launches Agent Studio — a workspace where AI agents plan, build, and launch campaigns across a team's existing stack, backed by over 200 billion real decisioning events. The 200B milestone gives agentic decisioning at scale a credible proof point, and the studio model signals how marketers will interact with AI agents going forward.

stories.head: 3 ways marketing automation platforms are being reinvented around customer context
stories.plain: MarTech maps three structural shifts replacing the old lead-funnel MAP model: platforms moving toward real-time customer context, agentic next-best-action, and outcome-based orchestration. Essential reading for anyone deciding which marketing automation category to buy into or build on, as the MAP category itself is being redefined.

stories.head: ZeroBounce launches first tool to detect AI-managed email inboxes
stories.plain: ZeroBounce can now flag whether an email inbox is controlled by an autonomous AI agent rather than a human. As AI agents increasingly handle business inboxes, marketers sending to those addresses face new deliverability and compliance questions. This is the first validation tool to address the problem, changing how email lists are cleaned and governed.

stories.head: AI workflows are exposing and amplifying bad marketing data
stories.plain: AI models inherit whatever is broken in your data pipeline — gaps, duplicates, stale records — and then act on them at scale. This piece shows how to audit your pipeline and fix problems at the source before they corrupt AI-driven personalization and decisioning. Foundational for anyone building or buying AI-powered marketing infrastructure.

stories.head: 98% of firms deploy AI in CX but only 15% achieve end-to-end agentic orchestration, Talkdesk report finds
stories.plain: Talkdesk's new State of Agentic Automation in CX report exposes a sharp orchestration gap: nearly every company has switched on some AI, but only a small fraction have connected it across departments to resolve customer problems without human hand-offs. That gap tells buyers and builders exactly where agentic AI investment is still failing.

stories.head: Auxia crosses 200B AI decisions and launches Agent Studio for coordinated marketing campaigns
stories.plain: Auxia's Agent Studio lets marketers direct AI agents that plan, build, and launch campaigns across existing martech stacks, drawing on full business context. The 200-billion-decision milestone gives the platform real credibility. It signals a shift toward purpose-built agentic layers sitting on top of — rather than replacing — current tools.

stories.head: The hidden cost trap: API fees and middleware can erase AI workforce savings
stories.plain: A MarTech analysis shows that autonomous agent API costs and middleware fees scale fast enough to wipe out the labour savings marketers expect. This is a must-read for anyone budgeting an agentic AI rollout — it reframes the ROI calculation that vendors rarely show and changes how AI is bought and governed.

stories.head: 3 ways marketing automation platforms are being reinvented around customer context
stories.plain: MarTech maps three structural shifts remaking the classic MAP: moving from lead-routing to real-time customer context engines, adding agentic decisioning layers, and integrating predictive next-best-action. Anyone evaluating or replacing a marketing automation platform needs this framework to understand what the category is becoming.

stories.head: ZeroBounce becomes first email platform to detect AI-managed mailboxes
stories.plain: ZeroBounce can now flag inboxes run by autonomous AI agents rather than real people, a new layer beyond standard bounce and spam-trap checks. As AI agents increasingly act as buyers, researchers, and approvers, knowing whether a recipient is human or bot changes how marketers target, measure, and govern their email programs.

themes.head: AI Deployment Outpacing Readiness
body: Companies are racing to ship AI into customer experience and content workflows before the underlying data quality, processes, or skills are in place to support it. The gap between deployment speed and operational readiness is widening, and AI is now exposing dirty data and broken workflows that were previously hidden by human workarounds.

The teams actually getting results share one habit: they systematically convert scattered AI experiments into documented, repeatable organizational advantages before scaling. The lesson is that implementation discipline — not model choice — separates winners from noise.

themes.head: The Rise of Agentic Marketing Infrastructure
body: A new layer of infrastructure is forming beneath the martech stack: agent orchestration platforms that coordinate AI workers alongside human ones. Auxia's Agent Studio and Tempo's Workforce Intelligence both launched this month, each positioning itself as an operating system for blended human-AI teams — complete with attribution logic that accounts for agentic output.

This signals a structural shift: marketing automation is no longer just about scheduling and routing; it is becoming a real-time decision fabric that allocates tasks across humans and autonomous agents and then measures ROI across both. Budget holders will soon need to account for agent headcount just as they account for human headcount.
ev: MarTech Series · Auxia Agent Studio 200B decisions

themes.head: AI-Native Brand Visibility as the New SEO
body: AI answer engines — Gemini, ChatGPT, Perplexity — are becoming primary discovery surfaces, and brands that have not structured their web presence for machine-readable citation are quietly disappearing from search results. Research shows business websites dominate Gemini's local citations, meaning owned content still matters, but the rules for what gets cited have changed fundamentally.

Marketers now need an AI discoverability strategy that sits alongside — or even above — traditional SEO: optimising for how agents retrieve and synthesise information, not just how crawlers index pages. The IAB's updated AI-in-ads disclosure standard adds a regulatory layer on top, making transparency about AI-generated content a compliance issue as well as a brand-trust issue.

themes.head: Measurement Reckoning: Incrementality Over Vanity
body: Attribution is under reconstruction. Multiple pieces this month converge on the same point: marketers have been measuring the wrong things, and AI is forcing the issue by making the cost of bad measurement visible at scale. The advice is consistent — run fewer, better-designed incrementality tests rather than a sprawl of low-confidence experiments, and treat post-campaign analysis as the starting point for the next campaign, not a post-mortem.

Adobe & Azira's cross-border footfall measurement launch and Tempo's human-vs-agent ROI attribution both reflect this pressure: every dollar now needs a defensible causal story, not a correlation. For teams new to the field, this means investing in measurement infrastructure before layering on more AI tools.

themes.head: Enterprise AI Partnership Consolidation
body: The biggest platforms are locking in deep partnerships — Bain with Anthropic, Cisco with NVIDIA, Docusign & Relativity with Google Cloud Gemini — to deliver AI not as a feature but as embedded enterprise infrastructure. This consolidation is compressing the window in which mid-market brands can choose best-of-breed freely; dominant stacks are forming fast around a handful of foundation models.

For martech buyers, the practical implication is that vendor ecosystem alignment is becoming a strategic decision, not just a procurement one. Choosing a CRM or data platform increasingly means implicitly choosing a foundation model and a cloud, with downstream consequences for data portability, compliance, and future AI capability access.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack this month, the decisive question is the same: whether organisations can build the operational discipline, data quality, and measurement rigour to keep pace with the AI capabilities they are already deploying.
